Dockerfile.text:
FROM node:22-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY store.mjs page.mjs widget.mjs server.mjs ./
RUN mkdir -p /data && chown node /data
USER node
ENV PORT=8080 STATE=/tmp/state.json
EXPOSE 8080
HEALTHCHECK CMD wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz || exit 1
CMD ["node", "server.mjs"]

README.md.text:
# testimonial-keeper

After using this, you can now **collect customer testimonials with a link, approve the ones you want, and show them as a wall on your own site**, on a server you own. That used to mean a monthly subscription to a testimonial service that keeps your customers' words behind its own login.

**Live tool:** https://duncan-haywood.github.io/monorepo-projects/testimonial-keeper/

Two parts, both free and MIT:

- **`index.html`**: the product page with a live demo of the embeddable wall (clearly labelled sample data). Runs in the browser; nothing is uploaded.
- **`server.mjs`**: the service. One Node process, **zero dependencies**, state in one JSON file. It serves the collection form, an admin page, a JSON API and the embed script.

## Why someone would use this

| Today | Cost / catch | Testimonial Keeper |
|---|---|---|
| Testimonial.to, Senja, Shoutout and similar | Paid tiers gate the number of testimonials, forms or the widget; the data lives with them | Unlimited forms and testimonials, one JSON file you own, no fee |
| A Google Form and copy-paste | No approval flow, no consent record, no widget | Consent tick stored with every entry, approve/hide, embeddable wall, CSV export |
| Screenshots of emails | Not verifiable, no permission, awkward to update | Customer-submitted words, shown only after approval, never edited |

Honest limits: **text only** (no video or image upload), one admin key (no per-user logins), no automatic import from G2, Trustpilot or social posts, no email sending of its own (set `NOTIFY_WEBHOOK` to get a Slack/ntfy ping instead), and no proof that a submitter is a real customer: it records what they typed and that they agreed to publish it.

## What it does

1. **Collection form** at `/t/<slug>`: name, optional role, company, 1-5 rating and email (never published), the testimonial (20-600 characters) and a **required consent tick** to publish. Honeypot field, a per-visitor daily cap (visitor keys are HMAC hashes, kept for the day and not stored with the testimonial) and a double-submit check.
2. **Moderation.** Everything starts *pending* and is invisible. Approve or hide in `/admin` (the admin key is typed into the page and sent as a bearer header; it is never in a URL). The text is never edited, only shown or not.
3. **The wall.** `<script src="https://<host>/embed.js" data-form="main" data-limit="12" data-theme="light" defer></script>` renders approved testimonials inside a shadow root using `textContent` only, so a testimonial cannot inject markup or restyle your page. `GET /wall.json?form=main` is the same data (CORS open) if you want your own layout.
4. **Reports and export.** `GET /v1/summary` (pending, approved, hidden, average rating of approved rated ones), `GET /v1/testimonials.csv` (spreadsheet formulas neutralised).
5. **Notifications.** `NOTIFY_WEBHOOK` receives `{"text": "..."}` for each new submission (works with Slack-compatible and many chat webhooks).

## Run it

```sh
cd ventures/testimonial-keeper
node --test        # 16 tests, no network
ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) PUBLIC_URL=https://proof.example.com COMPANY_NAME=Acme node server.mjs
```

A form named `default` is created on first start. Add more:

```sh
curl -s -X POST "$PUBLIC_URL/v1/forms" -H "authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" \
  -d '{"slug":"launch","title":"How did launch week go?","prompt":"What changed for you?"}'
```

| Env | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `ADMIN_KEY`, `PUBLIC_URL` | required |
| `COMPANY_NAME`, `BRAND_COLOR` | form wording and `#rrggbb` accent |
| `TRUST_PROXY` | `true` behind a reverse proxy so the per-visitor cap uses `X-Forwarded-For` (the Render blueprint sets it) |
| `IP_SECRET` | key for the daily visitor hash (random per start if unset) |
| `NOTIFY_WEBHOOK` | optional https webhook pinged on each submission |
| `STATE` | path of the JSON state file |

## One-click deploy (your own account)

Fork this repository and open `https://render.com/deploy?repo=<your fork URL>`. `render.yaml` builds the `Dockerfile` here in **your** Render account with a 1 GB disk and a generated `ADMIN_KEY`. Nothing runs on the author's side. Docker anywhere works: `docker build -t testimonial-keeper . && docker run -p 8080:8080 -v tk:/data -e STATE=/data/state.json -e ADMIN_KEY=... -e PUBLIC_URL=... testimonial-keeper`.

## Status and what is not verified

Everything in `node --test` passes, including the widget run against a fake DOM. It has **not** been tried in real browsers or at real traffic by the author. You are the operator: only publish what people agreed to, do not edit or invent testimonials, and follow the endorsement and review rules where you sell (for example the FTC rules in the US). Do not mark up your own testimonials as third-party review ratings in structured data: search engines treat self-collected reviews that way as self-serving.

Files: `store.mjs` (rules), `widget.mjs` (the embed), `page.mjs` (form and admin), `server.mjs` (HTTP shell), `index.html` (product page).

Support the project: <https://github.com/sponsors/Duncan-Haywood>.

## Other self-deploy paths

`docker-compose.yml` runs it on any box with Docker (the command is at its top). Fly.io: the steps are at the top of `fly.toml`. Both keep state on a volume and run in your own account.

name: testimonial-keeper
description: >-

  to write a testimonial with an explicit publish consent, an approve/hide
  admin page, and a shadow-DOM widget that shows only what you approved.
  Zero-dependency server with a one-click Render deploy.
stage: prototype
owner: duncan

# forms or widget use. The gap: a solo founder who wants unlimited forms, a
# stored consent record and the data in a file they own, with no per-seat fee.
# duplicate_check.py top score 0.20 (feedback-board collects feature requests,
# not publishable proof).
#
# First visitor: indie founders, freelancers, course creators on Indie Hackers,

#
# Path to revenue (payments stay off): free and MIT as the lead magnet; a hosted

fly.toml.text:
# Fly.io self-deploy, in your own account (needs flyctl and a card on file with Fly):
#   fly launch --copy-config --no-deploy --dockerfile Dockerfile
#   fly volumes create state --size 1
#   fly secrets set ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) IP_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 16)
#   (optional settings from render.yaml, e.g. PUBLIC_URL, go in with `fly secrets set` too)
#   fly deploy
# One machine that never auto-stops: the state file lives on its volume.
app = "testimonial-keeper-CHANGE-ME"
primary_region = "iad"

[build]
  dockerfile = "Dockerfile"

[env]
  PORT = "8080"
  STATE = "/data/state.json"
  TRUST_PROXY = "true"

[mounts]
  source = "state"
  destination = "/data"

[http_service]
  internal_port = 8080
  force_https = true
  auto_stop_machines = "off"
  auto_start_machines = false
  min_machines_running = 1
  [[http_service.checks]]
    path = "/healthz"
    interval = "30s"
    timeout = "5s"

index.html.text:
Ask your happy customers for a testimonial, and show the ones you approve

Send one link. Customers write a few lines and tick a box agreeing that you may publish them. You approve or hide each one, and a single script tag shows the approved ones on your site. It runs on your own server with the data in one file, so there are no tiers, no seat fees and no testimonial caps. Read the source or deploy it below.

The wall your visitors would see sample data

These three are invented to show the layout. Nobody said them. Your wall only ever contains what your customers submitted and you approved.

Why use this instead of what you do today

TodayCatchTestimonial Keeper
Testimonial.to, Senja, Shoutout and similarPaid tiers cap testimonials, forms or the widget; the data lives with themUnlimited, one JSON file you own, no fee
A Google Form and copy-pasteNo approval flow, no consent record, no widgetConsent stored per entry, approve/hide, embeddable wall, CSV export
Screenshots of emailsNo permission on record, awkward to updateCustomer-written words shown only after you approve

Honest limits: text only (no video), one admin key, no import from review sites, and it cannot prove a submitter is a real customer.

Run it yourself

git clone https://github.com/Duncan-Haywood/oss-monorepo && cd oss-monorepo/ventures/testimonial-keeper
ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) PUBLIC_URL=https://proof.example.com COMPANY_NAME=Acme node server.mjs

# share:   https://proof.example.com/t/default      (approve at /admin)
# embed:   <script src="https://proof.example.com/embed.js" data-form="default" defer></script>

One-click Render deploy and Docker are in the README.

Related tools

Grow with Cancel Flow to keep subscribers and Feedback Board to collect feature requests, and Review Reply Desk to answer the public reviews you get on Google.

Questions

Do customers have to agree before I publish?

Yes. The form has a required consent tick and the agreement is stored with each testimonial. Nothing is public until you approve it, and the text is never edited.

Where does the data live?

In one JSON file on the server you deploy in your own account. The author runs nothing in between and never sees your customers.

Can a testimonial hijack my page?

No. The embed renders inside a shadow root using textContent only, so a testimonial can never inject markup or restyle your page.

Does it support video?

Not yet. It is text and an optional 1-5 rating, which keeps it small enough to read in an evening.

Is it a review site?

No. It collects words from your own customers for your own site. Do not mark them up as independent third-party review ratings.

No warranty. This tool and the server are provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied, and with no uptime or delivery guarantee. You are the operator: publish only what people agreed to, never edit or invent testimonials, and follow the endorsement and consumer-protection rules where you sell. It is not legal, tax, or financial advice. The demo above runs in your browser: nothing you do is uploaded and the page makes no network requests. Usage counters (opt-out below) stay in your browser's local storage.

render.yaml.text:
# One-click self-deploy: https://render.com/deploy?repo=<your fork URL>
# Render builds the Dockerfile in YOUR account; nothing runs on the author's.
services:
  - type: web
    name: testimonial-keeper
    runtime: docker
    dockerContext: ventures/testimonial-keeper
    dockerfilePath: ventures/testimonial-keeper/Dockerfile
    plan: starter
    healthCheckPath: /healthz
    disk:
      name: state
      mountPath: /data
      sizeGB: 1
    envVars:
      - key: STATE
        value: /data/state.json
      - key: ADMIN_KEY
        generateValue: true
      - key: IP_SECRET
        generateValue: true
      - key: TRUST_PROXY
        value: "true"
      - key: PUBLIC_URL
        sync: false
      - key: COMPANY_NAME
        sync: false
      - key: BRAND_COLOR
        sync: false
      - key: NOTIFY_WEBHOOK
        sync: false
